clue.text: Light upon a record surplus? a

parts.note: a record, especially a gramophone one, is a disc
anything left over is surplus

explanation.surface: Someone notices that a record was in excess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light upon' means to come across by chance, so it is the definition. The final 'a' looks like a stray letter from the printed page and does nothing in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To light upon something is to find it by chance, a synonym for coming across it.

clue.text: Composer who exhibits extraordinary tameness

indicators.note: extraordinary suggests the letters of the next word are out of their ordinary order

explanation.surface: A musician is praised for showing remarkable docility.
explanation.definitionFit: Jules Massenet was a French composer of operas such as Manon.

clue.text: A man of French stock who enjoys a 6 across

definitions.text: A man of French stock who enjoys a 6 across

parts.words: A man of French stock who enjoys a 6 across
parts.note: seems to describe a man of French descent, but 'stock' means investments: a person living off French government bonds and so enjoying unearned income

explanation.surface: A Frenchman of good lineage enjoys money of his own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French stock' looks like ancestry; it is rentes, French government bonds, whose holders live on the interest. 6 across is PRIVATE INCOME.
explanation.definitionFit: A rentier is someone who lives on income from investments or property rather than work.

clue.text: Old Norse part of Manchester now up for grabs, apparently

parts.note: Sale is a town in Greater Manchester

explanation.surface: An old Viking district of Manchester is available to buy.
explanation.walkthrough: SALE is a town in Greater Manchester, in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods offered for purchase are available to anyone, hence up for grabs.

clue.text: Buffalo Bill going round the Middle East for light entertainment

indicators.note: going round means the showman's name encircles the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: Buffalo Bill was the nickname of the showman William Cody
ME is the usual abbreviation for the Middle East

explanation.surface: The Wild West showman tours the Middle East with his show.
explanation.definitionFit: Comedy is humorous entertainment, the lighter kind of drama.

clue.text: The lowest soldier can expect this to cushion his retirement?

definitions.text: The lowest soldier can expect this to cushion his retirement?

parts.words: The lowest soldier can expect this to cushion his retirement?
parts.note: the lowest rank in the army is a private, so what a private earns is wittily read as unearned money of one's own

explanation.surface: A humble soldier looks forward to some pension money.
explanation.walkthrough: The lowest soldier is a private; the phrase also means money from investments rather than wages.
explanation.definitionFit: Income from investments or inheritance, not employment, is unearned money that funds a comfortable life.

clue.text: Indoor spread that could set one back hundreds of pounds

definitions.text: Indoor spread that could set one back hundreds of pounds

parts.words: Indoor spread that could set one back hundreds of pounds
parts.note: an indoor spread is a floor covering, and a fine hand-knotted one from Iran is notoriously expensive

explanation.surface: Something laid out inside the home costs a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' suggests a meal or a bedspread; it is something spread on the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A handmade Iranian rug is a costly floor covering prized by collectors.

clue.text: Wily fellows shouldn't be caught taking it

definitions.text: Wily fellows shouldn't be caught taking it

parts.words: Wily fellows shouldn't be caught taking it
parts.note: a cunning person dodges capture by manoeuvring to escape, the steps one takes to avoid being caught

explanation.surface: Crafty people should never be found out doing it.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a moral about wily people; really, what they take is the manoeuvre that stops them being caught.
explanation.definitionFit: Manoeuvres made to avoid danger or capture are what crafty people use to escape.

clue.text: A summary of prices

indicators.note: of here means made out of, so the answer is formed from the letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A brief digest of what things cost.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no usual anagram word: 'of' means 'made from', so the summary is made from the letters of PRICES.
explanation.definitionFit: A précis is a short abstract of a text, a synonym for summary.

clue.text: The difference between imports and exports

definitions.text: The difference between imports and exports

parts.words: The difference between imports and exports
parts.note: a straight description of the shortfall when a country buys more abroad than it sells

explanation.surface: An economics definition of a balance gap.
explanation.definitionFit: The shortfall in a nation's balance of commerce when imports exceed exports.

clue.text: A priest that is round about fifty?

indicators.note: round means the abbreviation for that is surrounds the numeral
about indicates the assembled letters are turned backwards

parts.note: i.e. (id est) is the abbreviation for that is
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A clergyman who is roughly fifty years old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts L inside IE to give ILE, and 'about' turns that round. Eli is the priest at Shiloh in the Bible who raised Samuel.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Old Testament, Eli was the high priest of Shiloh and mentor of Samuel.

clue.text: Raving mad suggestion for a seaside holiday in Scotland

definitions.text: suggestion for a seaside holiday in Scotland

indicators.note: mad suggests the letters of the preceding word are deranged and rearranged

explanation.surface: A frenzied proposal for a beach break north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: Girvan is a seaside resort town on the Ayrshire coast of south-west Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Girvan is a Scottish coastal resort, so it is one place to propose for a holiday by the sea.

clue.text: All the things the lorimer turned out?

definitions.text: the things the lorimer turned out?

explanation.surface: Everything produced by the harness maker.
explanation.walkthrough: A lorimer makes bits, spurs and other metal parts for horses' bridles, so all he produced was every bit.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the whole of something, and a lorimer's products include bridle bits, every one of them.

clue.text: Corn-spirit?

explanation.surface: A spirit distilled from grain.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'corn' means any cereal crop, so it covers rye; rye is also a whiskey distilled from that grain.
explanation.definitionFit: The cereal grain grown for flour, and also the whisky distilled from it.

clue.text: Unappreciative person found among Reading ratepayers

indicators.note: found among says the answer lies within the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: An ungrateful taxpayer is discovered in the town of Reading.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading is an English town, which helps the surface; the answer runs from 'readING RATEpayers'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingrate is someone who shows no gratitude, an unthankful person.

clue.text: A record height to scale

parts.note: LP, long-playing, is a record

explanation.surface: A climber's record ascent.
explanation.definitionFit: An Alp is a high mountain, a peak for a climber to scale.

clue.text: Quarrels that may clear the air, perhaps

definitions.text: that may clear the air, perhaps

explanation.surface: Rows can be a good way to settle things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breeze' is informal British for a quarrel; breezes are also light winds that freshen the air.
explanation.definitionFit: In old slang a breeze is a row, and light winds literally freshen stale atmosphere.

clue.text: Mac's other name

parts.note: Mac looks like a Scotsman's nickname, but it is short for mackintosh, the waterproof coat

explanation.surface: What else a Scot called Mac goes by.
explanation.definitionFit: A mac or mackintosh is a waterproof coat worn in wet weather.

clue.text: No bad feeling?

parts.note: reads as an absence of ill will, but describes a feeling that is extremely good, a state of elation

explanation.surface: A reassurance that there is no resentment.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphoria is intense happiness, a feeling far from bad.

clue.text: A most awkward little child to put up with

indicators.note: awkward suggests the letters of the preceding words are clumsily jumbled

parts.note: ch is the abbreviation for child

explanation.surface: An extremely difficult toddler is hard to tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: To stomach something is to tolerate it, a synonym for bear.

clue.text: The principal events in a play hatched by mutinous seamen?

definitions.text: The principal events in a play

explanation.surface: A drama's storyline concerns a mutiny at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The main is the sea, so a scheme hatched at sea by mutineers is a main plot.
explanation.definitionFit: The central storyline of a drama, and also a conspiracy on the high seas.

clue.text: Indian meal — just a plain tea, B presumably?

definitions.text: just a plain tea, B presumably?

explanation.surface: A sparse afternoon meal without sweet things.
explanation.walkthrough: Nocake is parched maize meal eaten by Native Americans; read as two words it describes a plain tea. The 'B' looks like a stray mark from the printed page.
explanation.definitionFit: Nocake is a Native American food of parched ground maize, and a bare tea lacks any sweet bakes.

clue.text: Strange ordeal on the Rio Grande

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters of the next word take an odd new order

explanation.surface: An unusual trial takes place by the big river.
explanation.walkthrough: Laredo is a city in Texas on the Rio Grande, the river forming the US-Mexico border.
explanation.definitionFit: Laredo is a Texan border city lying beside the river separating the US and Mexico.

clue.text: Striking deed of minor devilry?

indicators.note: deed of devilry puts the deed second, so the devil comes first

parts.note: an imp is a minor devil
an act is a deed

explanation.surface: A mischievous little act that hits hard.
explanation.definitionFit: An impact is a collision, the force of one thing hitting another.

clue.text: Have one's winnings notified initially

indicators.note: initially asks for the first letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: A gambler announces their winnings.
explanation.definitionFit: To own something is to possess it, a synonym for have.

clue.text: A range of crumpets

indicators.note: of here means made out of, so the answer is formed from the letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A large assortment of teatime crumpets.
explanation.walkthrough: As with PRECIS, 'of' means 'made from': the range is made from the letters of CRUMPETS, a British teatime griddle cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectrum is a broad sweep of values or kinds, a synonym for range.

clue.text: A native labourer that is indifferent to start with

indicators.note: to start with places the word for indifferent at the front

parts.note: cool means unenthusiastic or indifferent
i.e. (id est) is the abbreviation for that is

explanation.surface: A local worker who is at first apathetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically the word, now offensive, denoted a hired unskilled worker in Asia.

clue.text: Obey a command to do secretarial work, possibly

explanation.surface: A secretary follows the boss's instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking orders and writing down spoken words for typing are both covered by the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Accepting orders from someone, and writing down words spoken for transcription, as a secretary does.
